newsitem.title: JAPAN: POLL-Japan prices seen flat to slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Japan prices seen flat to slightly higher.

text.p: Japanese consumer prices are likely to stay flat or edge slightly higher, but are still a long way from danger levels that would warrant a change in monetary policy, a Reuters poll of economists showed on Thursday.

Thirty-seven economists gave an average forecast of a 1.8 percent rise in consumer prices this business year, and 26 of them forecast, on average, that prices would rise 0.7 percent in fiscal 1998/99.
The survey was conducted from July 7 to July 9.
Economists said that, after excluding the significant effect of the recent rise in the consumption tax, underlying inflation was around 0.5 percent.
The sales tax was raised to five percent from three percent on April 1, the beginning of the fiscal year.

"It's basically flat, with only a slight rise expected to come from an increase in rents," said Kyohei Morita, an economist at Nomura Research, who cited a trend towards a bottoming out in housing prices.

Also cited by economists as contributing factors to low inflation were the general trend for many central banks to keep inflation under control and a domestic demand environment in Japan in which firms know that products will not sell if prices are raised.

Overall wholesale prices were similarly forecast to rise 1.9 percent this fiscal year. But for 1998/99 the average of forecasts was flat, as many economists saw a stronger yen putting downward pressure on prices.
